newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes down amid liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes down amid liquidity.

text.p: rates closed down 200 basis points at 21.80 percent on
Thursday in a market awash with liquidity, traders said.
"Rates took time to settle down, but they are low so any increases are short-lived and just anomalous trades," a trader said.
Dealers added that month-end demand for cash, which usually exerts pressure on rates, was offset by ample market liquidity.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.153 billion pesos in surplus
liquidity from the market during the session.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed off 50 basis points
Dealers said rates declined in line with a firmer peso.
Benchmark 48-hour pesos closed 0.9 of a centavo at

Expectations that the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm would announce no change in U.S. interest rates at its February 4 meeting have also dissipated upside pressure on Mexican secondary rates, dealers said. Primary rates are falling further in February.

A hefty 8.804 billion pesos of liquidity was expected to return to the system on Friday. Traders cautioned that month-end demand for cash and corporate tax bills falling due could drain some of that liquidity.
